job.organization: Hacienda La Puente Unified School District

items.item_text: 01. These supplemental questions are part of the selection process and are considered part of your application. These questions give you the opportunity to fully explain your background and qualifications as they pertain to this position. Read the following questions and respond to each question thoroughly and accurately. Your answers to the following supplemental questions are required for your application to be considered complete. All experience mentioned in the Supplemental Questions must also be included in the Work Experience section in order to be considered complete. A resume will not be accepted in lieu of completion of the required application or supplemental questions. Resumes are NOT reviewed, therefore information on the resume will not be considered in the screening of the application. NOTE: Be sure to respond honestly and truthfully to all questions. Applicants found to have provided false or misleading information will be disqualified from further consideration, or, if hired, may be terminated from employment. I have read and understand this statement. Options: Yes | No

02. Please identify your highest level of education obtained. Options: No high school diploma or educational equivalent (e.g. GED) | High school or equivalent (e.g. GED) | Some college coursework (12 or more semester units) | Associate's degree or higher

03. Proof of highest obtained education must be submitted by the final test part. You may upload the documents to your online application (in the "Attachments" section) at the time of application or fax them to Silvia Lagunas at (626) 631-3015. NOTE: If you have a foreign degree, it must be certified in the U.S. by an approved foreign credentials evaluation service provider. Candidates are responsible of ensuring the timely submission of the evaluation. Please note that foreign credential evaluation services typically take three to six weeks to provide evaluation reports. If you need a list of approved agencies, please contact us at 626-933-3920. I have read and understand this statement. Options: Yes | No

04. How many years of clerical work experience do you possess? In determining qualifying experience, applicants' part-time employment will only receive partial credit based on the number of hours worked per week. For example, a position that works 40 hours a week for one year would get one year of credit, whereas a position that works 20 hours a week for one year would get six months of credit. Options: No experience | Less than 3 years | At least 3 years, but less than 4 years | 4 years or more

05. In reference to the question above, please provide the following information for EACH organization where you gained clerical experience : 1) Your job title 2) Organization name 3) Start and end dates (month/year) and number of hours worked per week 4) Brief description of clerical-related duties Please write "N/A" if you do not have experience in this area. Do NOT type "see resume."
Possession of a valid California Class C Driver license.
Plans, organizes, and assists in a variety of personnel functions including job analysis, classification and compensation studies, recruitment, and employee development and training.

Communicates and responds to questions from administrators, employees, Human Resources staff and the public regarding classifications, selection, recruitments and other Personnel Commission matters with discretion and confidentiality.
Provides primary support to the Personnel Commission in the preparation and distribution of the Personnel Commission agendas, minutes and related matters.
Plans, coordinates, and conducts the employee recognition programs.
Assists in the scheduling, conducting, and coordinating of training presentations, new hire orientations and other Personnel Commission activities.
Plans, organizes and assists in the employment process for classified employees in compliance with Merit System rules.
Composes and prepares drafts of recruitment materials, and advertises and posts ads in various recruitment sources.
Coordinates examination logistics by securing necessary facilities, scheduling candidates, arranging rater panels, and copying and collating examination materials.
Responds to protests by examinees or refers to appropriate personnel.
Notifies applicants of status and results during recruitment processes.
Prepares and composes a variety of correspondence and reports.

Establishes, audits and maintains a variety of personnel files, databases, and records related to recruitment, selection, classification, training and other Personnel Commission related matters, according to established procedures, policies, rules and regulations.
Generates and compiles statistical results and drafts reports and recommendations.

Gathers, interprets, and provides information to employees, job applicants, school districts, outside agencies and the public regarding Education Code, Personnel Commission Rules, regulations, policies, and employment opportunities.
Operates an applicant management system and other computer systems to query, input, obtain data and produce reports.
Scores exams and processes applicant statistical data to generate a variety of reports including lists of candidate scores, item analysis, and compiling employment eligibility lists.
Ensures accuracy in hiring candidates from eligibility lists.
Assists in administrating job analysis questionnaires and other methodology used to conduct job analysis, salary surveys and classification studies.
Gathers and compiles data relative to salaries, classification, job analysis and related human resource issues.
Supervises or assigns duties to the Personnel Commission staff as needed.
Performs research projects of limited scope as assigned.
Drives a vehicle to various sites to conduct work as needed.
Assists in the development and construction of test materials as assigned.
Performs other related duties as directed.

Evidence of adequate insurance for a motor vehicle, which meets or exceeds the California legal liability insurance requirement and continue to maintain insurability. For those positions which require driving District vehicles, incumbents must be able to be insured, and continue to be insured, by the District's liability insurance carrier.
